translation_notes: the module's 14-name `from rdflib.namespace import (...)` block becomes 14 @prefix declarations (DC->dc, DCTERMS->dcterms, FOAF->foaf, ORG->org, OWL->owl, PROF->prof, PROV->prov, QB->qb, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, SDO->sdo, SH->sh, SKOS->skos, VANN->vann); this region only uses sdo:, the other thirteen are the file's, kept so the correspondence with the import block stays 1:1

SDO.domainIncludes -> sdo:domainIncludes inside graph.subjects(...), SDO.rangeIncludes -> sdo:rangeIncludes inside a list display: [sdo:rangeIncludes] transpiles as a one-element list of a URIRef, which is the residual-collision case documented in the language reference (a declared prefix wins over a slice reading) -- here that is exactly what is wanted, but it is worth flagging as the one spot where the ldpy reading of unchanged Python text differs
fixed a mechanical-draft bug: the @prefix block had been inserted in the middle of a parenthesised import, which is not valid ldpy; declarations now sit after all imports
no g{} island applies: the region reads a Dataset and builds Python dataclasses, it never constructs triples -- namespace terms are all the notation can reach here

context shim: pyLODE is not installed; context.py holds the model dataclasses (Profile, Property, Class, Resource, Ontology, ProfileType and unused stand-ins) and the query/common.py helpers copied verbatim from RDFLib/pyLODE@0d0471fb99. Import lines only, identical on both sides

driver builds a two-named-graph rdflib Dataset and a duck-typed Query; three fixtures (matches in both graphs, an ignored subclass, no match). The default graph is materialised up front because Dataset.contexts() otherwise creates it lazily and the region's nested get_graph() call trips rdflib's 'Set changed size during iteration' -- an rdflib quirk affecting both sides identically
